Maintaining Community Software

Community software survives when maintainers make expectations visible and give contributors a dependable way to participate.

A small issue template can explain what evidence is needed, while a focused review guide helps volunteers understand how decisions are made.

Release notes should describe user-visible changes in plain language so readers can decide whether an update affects their work.

Healthy projects also document how responsibilities are shared, because no single maintainer should become the only path for every decision.

These habits reduce uncertainty and let a project continue serving its users even as individual contributors change over time.
